Lakers Nation > Blog > Lakers News > Lakers News: JJ Redick Explains Why He Likes Jake LaRavia In Starting Lineup Lakers News Lakers News: JJ Redick Explains Why He Likes Jake LaRavia In Starting Lineup
 Matthew Valento Published: 11/14/2026 4 Min Read Nov 11, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Bucks guard Tyler Herro (11) looks for a shot against Los Angeles Lakers forward Jake LaRavia (12) in the third quarter at Fiserv Forum. Mandatory Credit: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images SHARE Establishing a consistent starting lineup has been an issue for the Los Angeles Lakers over the past few seasons. Head coach JJ Redick has often needed to maneuvere through injuries to key players, resulting in a lack of continuity.
 This year presents a new challenge with nine new players, so Redick has been experimenting and it appears Jake LaRavia may be a mainstay as a starter due to his rebounding.
 “Yeah, look, I mean sometimes you… This is a very extreme example,” Redick began. “So, I’m not comparing examples, but I’m giving you an example from my NBA experience and my NBA history. Our plan going into the 2008-2009 season was we get Rashard Lewis and Tony Battie was going to start and they were going to figure out what to do with Turk [Hedo Turkoglu]. And Tony Battie during not training camp, but during preseason in September, tore his labrum and we ended up starting Rashard and Turk. And we become this 4-out 1-in, spread pick-and-roll, become one of the top offenses in the league for a few seasons. Make a Finals, make a Conference Finals. 
 “So, sometimes things happen and you’re like, ‘Oh, we found something.’ Like Z [Ziaire Williams] gets hurt, we’re playing Miami. We’re playing against Giannis and Bam, we wanted another bigger body out there. So, we went with Jake and before that game we were 29th and 30th in rebounding percentage and second chance points. Since that game, we’ve been third and second. So, we’re up to 11th in second chance points, a lot of that has been Jake, a lot of that has been Walker. Those guys have been elite on the offensive glass for the last few games and we like that, he’s a bigger body. We joked with him this morning in our film session and all these guys and all their negative feedback, they were willing to take it. He’s fouling too much, think he’s P1 [first percentile] in fouls on shooting, giving up shooting fouls like he’s fouling too much. 
 “So, we still got stuff to clean up. Love what he’s doing on the offensive glass. Again, you’re going to have off shooting nights, if you can create second opportunities for yourself, that’s going to give you a chance to win.”
 LaRavia started some games last season and was projected to come off the bench this year. When Ziaire Williams got hurt though, LaRavia entered the starting lineup and that group clicked immediately. In 65 minutes together so far this season with LaRavia and the starters, the Lakers gave a ridiculous +30.7 net rating.
 Lineups will likely continue to change throughout the season based on effectiveness and injuries, but for now it makes sense for Redick to stick with this group based on how well they have played.
 JJ Redick emphasizes need for Lakers to keep improving after undefeated road trip
 The Lakers have enjoyed a much needed three-day break after their game against the Milwaukee Bucks. Despite an impressive 11-2 start, Redick is preaching that the team needs to continue improving .
